frs_sections.content:
85    Two main concerns are paramount for the I3C interface: The use of as little energy as possible in transporting
86    data and control, while reducing the number of physical pins used by the interface.
87    Therefore, the I3C interface features:
88     • Two wire serial interface up to 12.5 MHz using Push-Pull
89     • Legacy I2C Device co-existence on the same Bus (with some limitations)
90     • Dynamic Addressing while supporting Static Addressing for Legacy I2C Devices
91     • Legacy I2C messaging
92     • I2C-like Single Data Rate messaging (SDR)
93     • NOT SUPPORTED IN I3C BASIC: Optional High Data Rate messaging Modes (HDR)
94     • Multi-Drop capability
95     • Multi-Master capability
96     • In-Band Interrupt support
97     • Hot-Join support

protocol_overview.addressing: 7-bit slave address (Static for legacy I2C, Dynamic for I3C); Broadcast address 7'h7E; Hot-Join address 7'h02; per-CCC reserved-address restrictions per Table 9
protocol_overview.ninth_bit_semantics: T-Bit (Transition / Parity / End-of-Data) replaces I2C ACK on data bytes; address header still uses ACK/NACK

compliance_requirements: All I3C devices must respond to Broadcast Address 7'h7E and to their assigned Dynamic Address.
I3C Slaves shall NOT clock-stretch SCL (Slave-side clock stretching is not allowed on an I3C bus).
I3C Slaves shall implement an HDR Exit Pattern Detector even if they do not implement any HDR mode.
Every byte-write from Master uses 8 data + 1 T-Bit (odd parity = XOR(Data[7:0],1)); never an ACK from the Slave.
Every byte-read from Slave uses 8 data + 1 T-Bit acting as end-of-data (0=end, 1=continue).
Address-header ACK from Slave is Open-Drain on the 9th SCL bit, just like I2C.
On Mixed Fast Bus the SCL HIGH period during I3C frames must be ≤ tDIG_H_MIXED so Legacy I2C devices' 50 ns Spike Filter ignores I3C traffic.
Maximum SCL frequency in I3C Push-Pull SDR is 12.5 MHz (12.9 MHz absolute max).
Bus capacitance Cb per line ≤ 50 pF in I3C Push-Pull SDR.
Reserved addresses per Table 9 (7'h00, 7'h01, 7'h02, 7'h3E, 7'h5E, 7'h6E, 7'h76, 7'h7A, 7'h7C, 7'h7E, 7'h7F) shall not be used as Dynamic Addresses.

functional_requirements.text: SDA and SCL are bidirectional lines connected to a positive supply via pull-up resistors; when the bus is free both lines are HIGH.
Devices must use open-drain or open-collector output stages to perform the wired-AND function.
Data on SDA must be stable during the HIGH period of SCL; SDA may only change state while SCL is LOW.
A HIGH-to-LOW transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH defines a START condition (S).
A LOW-to-HIGH transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH defines a STOP condition (P).
A repeated START (Sr) is functionally identical to S; keeps the bus busy without an intervening STOP.
Every byte put on SDA must be 8 bits long; number of bytes per transfer is unrestricted; MSB-first.
Each byte is followed by a 9th ACK clock pulse generated by the master; receiver pulls SDA LOW to ACK, leaves SDA HIGH to NACK.
After START, master sends 7-bit slave address + 1-bit R/W direction; R/W=0 indicates write, R/W=1 indicates read.
Only the master may generate START, STOP, repeated START, and SCL clock pulses.
In multi-master systems, masters arbitrate bit by bit on SDA while SCL is HIGH; the first master to drive SDA HIGH when another drives LOW loses arbitration.
Clock synchronization is performed using the wired-AND on SCL; final SCL LOW period is determined by the master with the longest LOW, HIGH period by the master with the shortest HIGH.
Optional clock stretching: a slave can hold SCL LOW to extend the LOW period and force the master into a wait state.
Standard-mode (≤100 kbit/s), Fast-mode (≤400 kbit/s), Fast-mode Plus (≤1 Mbit/s), High-speed mode (≤3.4 Mbit/s), Ultra Fast-mode (≤5 Mbit/s) are supported.
Input reference levels are 30% (VIL = 0.3 VDD) and 70% (VIH = 0.7 VDD) of VDD; legacy fixed-level devices were VIL=1.5 V / VIH=3.0 V.

error_response_conditions: S0 — Invalid Broadcast Address or CCC code (slave shall ignore address mismatches at S0)
S1 — CCC code parity error (Slave shall NACK)
S2 — Write Data parity error (Slave shall NACK at the next byte boundary)
S3 — Read Data parity error (Slave shall set T=0 to end the read; Master detects)
S4 — Slave-driven monitor error during read
M0 — Master detects unexpected NACK / no addressed slave
M1 — Master detects invalid CCC return / optional
M2 — Master detects bus error (e.g. SDA stuck) and escalates to recovery
